chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from whom he mentioned, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him)

Regarding the umm al-walad (concubine who bore her master's child), when her master dies having made a bequest to her, he said: 'She is freed from the one-third [of the estate], and the bequest is hers.'

key_terms.أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ: Umm al-walad; a female slave who bore her male owner a child
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: The third; referring to the one-third of the estate available for bequests

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a concubine who bore her master's child when he dies and left her a bequest?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida clarifies that an 'umm al-walad' is manumitted from the one-third portion of the estate reserved for bequests, ensuring her freedom is prioritized within the testator's discretionary gifts. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that her emancipation is treated as a specific bequest rather than a debt, distinguishing it from the general distribution of the remaining two-thirds. The hadith underscores the importance of fulfilling the master's explicit wish for her liberation while maintaining the structural integrity of the inheritance division.
